findings.message: effect is created without a reactive owner; nothing will ever dispose it, so it keeps running and holding its subscriptions for the lifetime of the app
findings.hint: Create effects inside a component or computation so their owner disposes them. For deliberate module-scope reactivity, wrap the setup in createRoot(dispose => ...) and keep the dispose handle.

findings.message: accessor setter "setKind" is called inside owned scope dynamicComponent compute; writes under a children-capable owner create feedback loops in the reactive graph, and Solid throws REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE here in dev
findings.hint: Derive the value instead of writing it back: replace compute-then-set with a createMemo. If the write is genuinely imperative, move it to an event handler, an action, the apply function of createEffect(compute, apply), or a leaf scope (onSettled, createTrackedEffect). Wrapping the write in untrack() does not help: the guard keys on the owner, not on tracking. For an internal reactive signal only, opt in with { ownedWrite: true } in that signal's creation options; a store setter has no such opt-in.

findings.message: effect is created without a reactive owner; nothing will ever dispose it, so it keeps running and holding its subscriptions for the lifetime of the app; the enclosing callback is written under an owner but is handed on, stored or a class member that solid-checker cannot follow to its calls, so no owner is proven current when it runs
findings.hint: Create effects inside a component or computation so their owner disposes them. For deliberate module-scope reactivity, wrap the setup in createRoot(dispose => ...) and keep the dispose handle. Call the callback where the owner is current, or create its owner inside it (createRoot, runWithOwner with a captured getOwner()).

findings.message: dynamicComponent() is called with { static: true } and a source that is an async function, which always returns a Promise; the static form calls the source once and renders what it returns synchronously, so the dev builds throw "dynamic(): a static source must resolve synchronously, not to a promise" here and the production builds render nothing
findings.hint: Drop static: true so dynamicComponent() settles the source in its memo (and render it under a <Loading> boundary), or resolve the component before calling dynamicComponent() and pass a synchronous source.

findings.message: reactive accessor "read" is read directly in DynamicOnlyBody, which does not track; the read sees the current value once and never updates when "read" changes; this code is in a function that returns JSX but is also handed to code that may call it as a plain function, so whether it runs as a component is not proven
findings.hint: Move the read into a tracking scope: JSX, a createMemo, or the compute function of createEffect(compute, apply). If a one-time snapshot is intended, wrap the read in untrack() to make that explicit. No strict-read window is open for this read (a map function opens one only when the call passes a `name`), so Solid's development warning does not point out the stale value.

findings.message: reactive accessor "read" is read in MixedDynamicBody, but no compiler or semantic fact places where this code runs (tracked, untracked, in a callback, or never), so whether this read is untracked cannot be proven either way
findings.hint: Move the read into a tracking scope: JSX, a createMemo, or the compute function of createEffect(compute, apply). If a one-time snapshot is intended, wrap the read in untrack() to make that explicit. If this read executes untracked in dev, Solid warns STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED for it; this finding does not establish that it does, so confirm the read's actual execution and tracking status before relying on that warning.

findings.message: flush() is called in a function that runs where no call edge places it, and this program steps an action's body; if a step is on the stack when it runs, the installed @solidjs/signals throws FLUSH_IN_ACTION in dev, and in production the call drains nothing
findings.hint: Call flush() only from code proven outside every action body (an event handler that starts no action, a timer), or remove it: an action's writes commit when the action settles.
